stories.title: 29-year-old ‘endangered’ woman located safely at Southfield hospital
stories.summary: Christian Cook, a 29-year-old Southfield woman reported missing since Sept. 13, has been located safely at a local hospital, police said. She is receiving appropriate medical care, and authorities thanked the community for their help during the search. Search efforts included drone units, search rescue teams, and a K-9 unit.

photo.alt: Courtesy of Southfield Police Department

stories.title: A constitutional convention to limit abortion rights? Democrats push back on DeBoyer suggestion
stories.summary: Michigan Republican Rep. Jay DeBoyer proposed using a constitutional convention to reintroduce abortion restrictions, sparking backlash from Democrats and reproductive rights groups. Democratic lieutenant governor nominee Winnie Brinks and advocacy organizations condemned the remarks, emphasizing that abortion rights are already enshrined in Michigan's constitution through voter-approved amendments.

photo.alt: Michigan House Oversight Committee Chair Rep. Jay DeBoyer (R-Clay Township) talks to reporters on continuing allegations of ethics violation by Michigan Attorney General Dana Nessel. Dec. 16, 2025

stories.title: A Data Center on the Huron River: Ypsilanti Township Pushes Back
stories.summary: A proposed $1.25 billion research computing center by the University of Michigan and Los Alamos National Laboratory on a 144-acre site in Ypsilanti Township has sparked significant community backlash. Residents and local officials are raising concerns about environmental impact, water usage, and the project's effect on the community, leading to a 60-day moratorium on data center construction in the city.

source.name: By Sadie Jacobson, Alice VanderVliet, Alden Koschmann, Caroline Mathern, Roshan Malani, Lucas Oorbeck, Mia Benjey, and Adam Cameron
source.publication: The Communicator (Ann Arbor Community High School)

stories.title: A hard row to hoe: Detroit Farm and Cider owner
stories.summary: Leandra King, owner of Detroit Farm and Cider, is selling her property after years of disputes with the city, including criminal charges, code violations, and the seizure of animals. The city's recent actions prompted her to list the property for $5.3 million.

photo.alt: A “Marathon, Michigan Made, Detroit Driven” billboard looms over a dense industrial area with smoke pouring out of a stack.

stories.title: A Millage to Keep Metro Detroit's Stories Alive
stories.summary: A proposed Wayne and Oakland county millage aims to provide sustainable funding for the Detroit Historical Society and Charles H. Wright Museum of African American History. The measure would offer free admission for county residents, transportation assistance for students and seniors, teacher curriculum resources, and funding for smaller public historical museums. The proposal, listed as the Southeast Michigan Historical Museums Authority on the ballot, seeks to ensure the institutions' long-term viability while expanding access to Detroit's history.

photo.alt: Detroit Historical Society and Charles H. Wright Museum of African American History

stories.title: A Pretty Sweet Victory
stories.summary: Sonntag's team, specializing in baked goods, expanded their skills using unfamiliar ingredients like jicama to win the Foodtastic competition. They returned to Michigan as champions, with Sonntag planning to grow her business and express gratitude for her mentors. The team appears in episodes four and 11 of Foodtastic on Disney+.

photo.alt: Orin Jewlers Sept 2026 Ad

stories.title: Advocates, moms and lawmakers push for group prenatal care as Legislature weighs insurer issues
stories.summary: Advocates, mothers, and lawmakers in Michigan are promoting group prenatal care through the Centering Pregnancy program, emphasizing its benefits for maternal and infant health. Legislation requiring insurance coverage for group prenatal care has been introduced, with bipartisan support for bills targeting both Medicaid and private insurers.

photo.alt: Sen. Stephanie Chang speaking at an event in Lansing about group prenatal care legislation.

stories.title: Agnes in West Village Opening
stories.summary: Agnes, a new neighborhood restaurant in West Village, will be led by the team behind Selden Standard. The spot will focus on community-driven dining, though details remain limited as of late 2026.

photo.alt: Agnes in West Village Opening

stories.title: Amway and affiliates agree to pay $225 million to settle lawsuit over alleged deception of workers
stories.summary: Amway, based near Grand Rapids, Michigan, and two affiliates have agreed to a $225 million settlement with the FTC to resolve claims of deceiving workers by inflating product sales numbers and false earnings projections. The FTC alleges that most participants spent more on Amway products and training than they earned, while Amway disputes the FTC's characterization of its business practices.

photo.alt: Amway's world headquarters in Ada, Michigan, about 10 miles from Grand Rapids. (Dustin Dwyer / Michigan Radio)

stories.title: Ann Arbor for Public Power’s ballot proposal will be in voters’ hands in November — here’s what to know
stories.summary: Ann Arbor for Public Power gathered over 5,000 signatures to place a utility governance proposal on the 2026 midterm ballot, aiming to replace DTE Energy’s electrical utility with a city-run power grid. If approved, voters would elect a public utility board by 2028 to guide a transition to collective ownership. The proposal faces opposition from DTE-funded groups and concerns about costs, with estimates suggesting a $1 billion upfront expense for the city.

photo.alt: Petition to replace DTE with Public Power will hit the ballot this November

stories.title: Ann Arbor Hands-On Museum Closed for Scheduled Maintenance September 14-18
stories.summary: The Ann Arbor Hands-On Museum will be closed from September 14 to 18 for scheduled maintenance, with normal operations resuming on September 19. The museum's mission focuses on inspiring curiosity and exploration in STEM and the natural world.

photo.alt: Ann Arbor Hands-On Museum Closed for Scheduled Maintenance September 14-18

stories.title: Ann Arbor Photographer and Local Author releases 16th Novel for Deaf Awareness Week
stories.summary: Local Michigan author Paul Michael Peters’ new book, “The Rhythm is Going to Get You,” blends post-apocalyptic, dystopian, and survivalist science fiction while highlighting the heroic nature of the Deaf community. The novel is released for Deaf Awareness Week.

stories.title: Anti-ICE coalition asks Slotkin to help end ICE use of county jails for detention in Michigan
stories.summary: A Michigan-based coalition has sent a letter to U.S. Sen. Elissa Slotkin demanding action to end the use of county jails for ICE detention. The letter requests congressional oversight visits, release of withheld records, and support for state legislation to ban such contracts. Four Michigan counties currently house ICE detainees, with Calhoun County holding the most.

photo.alt: Coalition to Shut the Camps protest against ICE detention facilities in Michigan

stories.title: Antrim County Board of Commissioners and virtual comments
stories.summary: Antrim County's Board of Commissioners eliminated remote participation several years ago, which became a point of controversy during an election. While this decision aimed to prevent meeting disruptions, it also affected residents with mobility challenges who must attend in person.

photo.alt: A “Marathon, Michigan Made, Detroit Driven” billboard looms over a dense industrial area with smoke pouring out of a stack.

stories.title: Arthur Lupia Retires as Vice President for Research and Innovation
stories.summary: Arthur Lupia, a political science scholar and leader in research innovation, retires after transforming U-M's research initiatives. As vice president, he launched programs like Bold Challenges and the Impact Institutes. His academic work on voter behavior and science communication earned him fellowships and awards, including the Guggenheim and Carnegie Fellowships.

source.name: University of Michigan Museum of Natural History

photo.alt: University of Michigan campus

stories.title: As enrollments plummet, Michigan communities sweat job losses from universities
stories.summary: Michigan's public universities face enrollment declines and limited state funding, leading to potential job losses and economic impacts on communities. Dan Hurley of the Michigan Association of State Universities highlights the long-term demographic challenges and financial pressures affecting regional campuses. Preliminary data from Central Michigan University shows a 4.6% enrollment drop, with similar trends reported at universities nationwide.

photo.alt: Daniel Hurley headshot

stories.title: As enrollments plummet, Michigan communities sweat job losses from universities
stories.summary: Michigan's public universities face enrollment declines and stagnant state funding, leading to potential job losses and economic impacts. Regional universities, excluding top-tier institutions like Michigan State and the University of Michigan, have seen significant drops in enrollment due to demographic shifts. This financial strain has prompted layoffs and cost-cutting measures at universities nationwide, with Michigan's institutions warning of long-term economic consequences for the state.

photo.alt: An empty street, lined with businesses.

stories.title: Auchter: Challenges ahead
stories.summary: Abdul El-Sayed faces challenges as a progressive Democrat avoiding the 'socialist' label, while Mike Rogers must navigate aligning with MAGA despite his traditional GOP background. Both candidates encounter political and ideological hurdles in their Senate race.

photo.alt: John Auchter / For Michigan Public

stories.title: Audit finds fault in Michigan job training program, claims $59M misspent
stories.summary: A state audit revealed that $59 million from Michigan's Going Pro Talent Fund was used for on-the-job training and orientation instead of education to boost worker skills and wages. The audit criticized the Department of Labor and Economic Opportunity for lax documentation and oversight, while the state contested the findings, defending the program's effectiveness despite budget cuts.

photo.alt: Audit finds fault in Michigan job training program, claims $59M misspent

stories.title: Audit finds fault in Michigan job training program, claims $59M misspent
stories.summary: A state audit revealed that one-third of $182.5 million in Michigan's Going Pro job training program was spent on employee orientation instead of education to boost skills and wages. The Department of Labor and Economic Opportunity faced criticism for lax oversight, while the state contested the findings, defending on-the-job training as a valid method. The program's budget has declined significantly, with the 2027 allocation at $14.4 million, a 40% drop from the previous year.

photo.alt: Audit finds fault in Michigan job training program, claims $59M misspent

stories.title: Aurora Italiana Opening in Detroit
stories.summary: Aurora Italiana, the third location of the upscale Italian chain, will open downtown Detroit. The restaurant will share a vibe with the group's existing Sexy Steak, offering colorful, hospitality-forward Italian cuisine.

photo.alt: Aurora Italiana Opening in Detroit

stories.title: Back on Top of Region XII
stories.summary: Schoolcraft College's men's and women's soccer teams both defeated St. Clair, securing their dominance at the top of Region XII. The women's team won 2-1 with goals from Summer Larson and Emily Williamson, while the men's team triumphed 2-1 with key contributions from Devlin McGinnis and Faisal Nasrallah. Both victories reestablished the Ocelots as the region's top program.

photo.alt: Schoolcraft College soccer players celebrating a goal during the match against St. Clair.

stories.title: Ballot question questions: Proof of citizenship
stories.summary: Michigan's Supreme Court blocked a November ballot measure requiring proof of citizenship to vote. Voters will decide on a proposal to restrict utility spending on political campaigns, with Bridge Michigan providing a fact-check to aid decision-making.

photo.alt: A “Marathon, Michigan Made, Detroit Driven” billboard looms over a dense industrial area with smoke pouring out of a stack.

stories.title: Benson, James pitch tariff remedies, business boosts & data center limits at Detroit Economic Club
stories.summary: Democratic gubernatorial nominee Jocelyn Benson and Republican nominee John James addressed the Detroit Economic Club on September 16, 2026, outlining their plans to address Trump-era tariffs, economic development, and data center regulations. Benson proposed subnational agreements with Canada to mitigate federal policies, while James advocated for using tariff revenue to reduce costs. Both emphasized local control over data centers and improving Michigan's competitiveness with neighboring states.

photo.alt: Jocelyn Benson and John James speaking at Detroit Economic Club event about tariffs and economic policies

stories.title: Big House advertisements draw mixed reactions from Michigan fans
stories.summary: The University of Michigan introduced advertisements at Michigan Stadium for the first time in its 99-year history, partnering with Coca-Cola, Meijer, and Google Gemini to generate revenue for student-athlete contracts. While some fans and alumni support the move to offset costs and remain competitive, others criticize the ads, particularly those for AI-related brands like Gemini, citing concerns over commercialization and environmental impact. The decision has sparked debate about the evolving role of sponsorships in college athletics.

photo.alt: Big House advertisements draw mixed reactions from Michigan fans

stories.title: Board of Police Commissioners rescinds virtual comment ban
stories.summary: Commissioner Henrietta Ivey rescinded her motion to end virtual public comments at Board of Police Commissioners meetings after public outcry. The board shortened comment times to 90 seconds, ensuring accessibility for people with disabilities.

photo.alt: A “Marathon, Michigan Made, Detroit Driven” billboard looms over a dense industrial area with smoke pouring out of a stack.

stories.title: Can Wayne County’s behavioral health system recover?
stories.summary: Wayne County's behavioral health system faces challenges including a proposed FY 2027 budget with uncertain Medicaid rates, significant revenue shortfalls, and the removal of Kenya Ruth from the DWIHN Board of Directors for misconduct. The system must address funding gaps for operations and a $60 million crisis center while navigating federal policy changes.

photo.alt: A “Marathon, Michigan Made, Detroit Driven” billboard looms over a dense industrial area with smoke pouring out of a stack.

stories.title: CANCELED – Sol Beats Beach Fiesta presented by Diversified Members Credit Union
stories.summary: The Sol Beats Beach Fiesta presented by Diversified Members Credit Union, scheduled for September 19 from 6:00 pm to 10:00 pm, has been canceled due to forecasted inclement weather. The event was part of the Beach Parties at Campus Martius Park series.

photo.alt: CANCELED – Sol Beats Beach Fiesta presented by Diversified Members Credit Union

stories.title: Cass Cafe Reopening in Detroit
stories.summary: Cass Cafe, a beloved Cultural Center staple, is set to reopen after closing four years ago. The Chalfonte Foundation, a Detroit-based nonprofit, is reviving the restaurant as a community space with a full bar, artwork, and nutritious meals.

photo.alt: Cass Cafe Reopening in Detroit

stories.title: City inspectors survey tornado damage
stories.summary: Detroit city inspectors say the tornado that hit the east side and Belle Isle on Sept. 3 damaged more than 100 homes and businesses. Nine buildings require emergency demolition. Mayor Mary Sheffield declared a local state of emergency to seek disaster relief money and coordinate with the Red Cross to assist families needing food and housing. City agencies have removed almost 300 fallen trees, hauled away more than 300 tons of debris, and restored 100 traffic signals.

photo.alt: Tornado damage in Detroit

stories.title: Consumers Energy asks state regulators to delay decision on hydroelectric dam sale until November
stories.summary: Consumers Energy has requested the Michigan Public Service Commission to delay its decision on the sale of 13 hydroelectric dams until November 9, 2026. The company cited the need for additional time to address concerns raised during the case proceedings. The request was not included in the commission’s September 2026 agenda.

photo.alt: Foote Dam in Iosco County, one of 13 hydroelectric dams proposed for sale by Consumers Energy. (Photo from Consumers Energy)

stories.title: Consumers will eventually pay the price for record-high diesel fuel
stories.summary: AAA Michigan reports record-high diesel fuel prices in the state, reaching $6.54 per gallon. The Trump administration's military actions in Iran have disrupted oil tanker traffic through the Strait of Hormuz, contributing to rising costs. Businesses are adjusting strategies, but increased expenses will likely be passed to consumers through higher prices.

photo.alt: Diesel fuel pump at a gas station

stories.title: Cooking and Combat: A Career Shaped by Two Passions
stories.summary: Chef Steve Yu at Schoolcraft College balances his roles as Executive Chef in Culinary Operations and Taekwondo instructor, combining discipline from both fields to foster success in students through patience, practice, and respect. His dual expertise in martial arts and culinary arts shapes his leadership style and teaching philosophy.

photo.alt: Executive Chef Steve Yu in the Culinary Operations kitchens at Schoolcraft College

stories.title: Critters Up Close
stories.summary: The Leslie Science & Nature Center is hosting a 'Critters Up Close' event. Visitors can check the dedicated page for upcoming dates and details about the program.

photo.alt: Critters Up Close

stories.title: Department of Public Safety hosts bike registration events for students
stories.summary: Eastern Michigan University's Department of Public Safety is hosting free bike and scooter registration events for students on Sept. 15 and Sept. 21. Registration requires completing a form with personal and vehicle details, and participants will receive identification stickers. The first three registrants at each event will get a free U-lock, and registered owners can report stolen vehicles using the recorded serial numbers.

photo.alt: Department of Public Safety hosts bike registration events for students

stories.title: Detroit Election Commission's 2-minute meeting
stories.summary: The Detroit Election Commission conducted all its business in a record 2-minute meeting, raising questions about the efficiency of November's election preparations.

photo.alt: A “Marathon, Michigan Made, Detroit Driven” billboard looms over a dense industrial area with smoke pouring out of a stack.

stories.title: Detroit Evening Report: Hundreds of people may be denied Flint settlement money due to paperwork errors
stories.summary: Hundreds of people who qualified for a share of the multi-million-dollar Flint water settlement fund may soon be cut out. That’s because some claims do not include correct Social Security numbers, or required signatures. Last week, a federal judge authorized sending final notices to thousands of claimants, advising them that unless they provide the missing information within 30 days their claim will be denied and closed.

photo.alt: Flint water crisis image

stories.title: Detroit family says woman was mistakenly cremated before funeral viewing
stories.summary: The family of Kimberlly Moore claims her body was accidentally cremated by Hutchison Funeral Home before her scheduled viewing, leading to a demand for answers. The funeral home has initiated an internal investigation and stated they will address the issue if found at fault.

photo.alt: Detroit family says woman was mistakenly cremated before funeral viewing

stories.title: Detroit Tenants Union Lawsuit Challenges Evictions and Compliance Requirements
stories.summary: A lawsuit by the Detroit Tenants Union challenges the requirement of a certificate of compliance for evictions, with landlords arguing it could collapse the rental market. The union and legal representatives argue unsafe housing should not be justified by economic constraints. The next hearing is set for September 21, 2026.

photo.alt: A row of older red-brick-and-wood houses with porches and trees line the street under a gray, overcast sky. Photo credit: Cydni Elledge/Outlier Media

stories.title: Early spark fades as Eastern Michigan Football drops road contest at Wisconsin, 54-10
stories.summary: The Eastern Michigan University football team started strong with an early lead but was overwhelmed by Wisconsin's explosive second-half performance, resulting in a 54-10 loss. Despite initial defensive success and a touchdown drive, the Badgers outscored the Eagles 28-0 in the second quarter and added 13 points in the fourth to secure the victory.

photo.alt: Eastern Michigan vs Wisconsin football game

stories.title: Eastbound I-94 in Wayne County closed for jackknifed semi-truck
stories.summary: Eastbound I-94 is closed Saturday, Sept. 19, at Michigan Avenue in Dearborn after a semi-trailer truck jackknifed, state police said.

photo.alt: Eastbound I-94 in Wayne County closed for jackknifed semi-truck

stories.title: EMU President Dr. Brendan Kelly uses investiture to focus on student achievement and well-being
stories.summary: A large crowd of students, faculty, staff, and alumni attended the investiture of Dr. Brendan Kelly as Eastern Michigan’s 24th President. During his address, Kelly emphasized the importance of focusing on student success and well-being, stating that universities must engage students as individuals to help them thrive in a disconnected, digital world.

photo.alt: Dr. Brendan Kelly addresses the crowd at his investiture on September 18, 2026.

stories.title: EMU Theatre welcomes two new faculty members: Heather Brown, Nikki Green
stories.summary: Eastern Michigan University Theatre is welcoming two new professors this semester: Heather Brown, a visiting professor of lighting design with over 25 years of experience, and Nikki Green, an assistant professor of costume design who previously worked at Disney World. Brown aims to expand the lighting design program to include corporate event production, while Green brings expertise in theatrical intimacy education and regional design experience.

photo.alt: EMU Theatre welcomes two new faculty members: Heather Brown, Nikki Green

stories.title: EMU to officially induct Brendan Kelly as president
stories.summary: Eastern Michigan University will hold the presidential investiture of Brendan Kelly on September 18, 2026, at 2 p.m. in Pease Auditorium. The ceremony, hosted by the EMU Board of Regents, will officially induct Kelly as the university's 24th president. Kelly began serving as president on April 1, 2026, succeeding James Smith after 10 years in the role.

photo.alt: EMU to officially induct Brendan Kelly as president

stories.title: Ever wonder how the Fed's interest rate actually works? We've got answers
stories.summary: The Federal Reserve raised interest rates by a quarter percentage point to combat accelerating inflation, increasing borrowing costs across the economy. This decision, the first this year, aims to slow economic activity and reduce inflationary pressures, impacting everything from mortgages to consumer loans.

source.name: Rafael Nam, Scott Horsley, Alina Selyukh, Stephan Bisaha

photo.alt: Federal Reserve interest rate hike intended to slow inflation and borrowing costs

stories.title: Federal judge dismisses lawsuit over Title X grant funding for pregnancy prevention efforts
stories.summary: A federal judge has dismissed a lawsuit regarding Title X grant funding for pregnancy prevention efforts.

photo.alt: Federal judge dismisses lawsuit over Title X grant funding for pregnancy prevention efforts

stories.title: Festival of Oddities to move. Organizer says Charlotte is unwelcoming
stories.summary: The organizer of the Festival of Oddities has announced the event will no longer be held in Charlotte due to harassment by a local religious group and inadequate support from city officials. Jenn Carpenter, a founder, cited safety concerns and a lack of police response during protests by a church group using megaphones to confront attendees. The festival, which ran at Charlotte's courthouse square since 2019, most recently took place Sept. 5-6, 2026, and is now seeking new hosts in Mid-Michigan.

photo.alt: Portrait of Dan Basso

stories.title: Former Michigan House speaker slated for Sept. 21 trial amid accusations of misusing political funds
stories.summary: Former Michigan House Speaker Lee Chatfield faces a Sept. 21 trial on 13 felony charges, including embezzlement and misuse of funds from political action committees and the Peninsula Fund. His wife, Stephanie, was recently sentenced to probation and fines after pleading guilty to embezzling from the Peninsula Fund. The investigation, which began in 2021, also included allegations of sexual assault, though those charges were dropped due to insufficient evidence.

photo.alt: Lee Chatfield and his wife Stephanie leaving court after their preliminary exam on Feb. 28, 2025.

stories.title: Funeral home launches internal review after woman was mistakenly cremated
stories.summary: Hutchison Funeral Home has launched an internal review after the family of Kimberlly Moore, who died from endometrial cancer, discovered her body was mistakenly cremated before a scheduled viewing. The family arrived for the Sept. 18 viewing but found another woman's body prepared, with conflicting information about whether Moore's ashes are available. The funeral home apologized and pledged to investigate the error.

photo.alt: Isaiah Hall headshot

stories.title: Generations of Southwest Detroit women demand pollution approaches
stories.summary: Residents in Southwest Detroit, a predominantly Black and Latino community, are advocating for new approaches to address long-standing pollution issues linked to industrial activity in the area.

photo.alt: A “Marathon, Michigan Made, Detroit Driven” billboard looms over a dense industrial area with smoke pouring out of a stack.

stories.title: High stakes embezzlement case against former GOP Michigan House speaker goes to trial next week
stories.summary: The trial of former Michigan House Speaker Lee Chatfield for alleged financial crimes is set to begin on Sept. 22, 2026. Chatfield faces 13 felony charges, including embezzlement from a nonprofit, and has pleaded not guilty. His attorney claims the case is politically motivated, while the prosecution alleges he used nonprofit funds for personal expenses and kickbacks. Stephanie Chatfield and two associates have already pleaded guilty and may testify against him.

photo.alt: Image from Michigan Advance

stories.title: High stakes embezzlement case against former GOP Michigan House speaker goes to trial next week
stories.summary: Former Michigan House Speaker Lee Chatfield faces 13 felony charges, including embezzlement from a nonprofit, in a trial set to begin Sept. 22. The case, which could mark a significant moment in Attorney General Dana Nessel’s tenure, involves allegations of using funds from the Peninsula Fund to finance a lavish lifestyle and political kickbacks. Chatfield has pleaded not guilty, with his defense claiming the charges are politically motivated.

photo.alt: Graphic by Susan J. Demas and photo by Andrew Roth depicting the embezzlement case against Lee Chatfield.

stories.title: Highgrade Deli Reopening in Detroit
stories.summary: Highgrade Deli, a longtime Corktown sandwich spot, is reopening this fall after being in receivership. The new owner, who previously operated Mike's Ham Place, will collaborate with original staff to revive the beloved deli.

photo.alt: Highgrade Deli Reopening in Detroit

stories.title: Homecoming dance canceled at Otsego High School due to threat
stories.summary: Otsego High School canceled its homecoming dance after receiving a threat, though students and staff were confirmed safe. The event was rescheduled with an unknown new date while investigations continue.

photo.alt: Police lights MLive

stories.title: Honors College students celebrate Shakespeare with annual Stratford Festival trip
stories.summary: Eastern Michigan University's Honors College takes students to the Stratford Festival in Stratford, Ontario, Canada, for two days of Shakespearean theater and cultural exploration. This year's trip is scheduled for Oct. 2-3, 2026, featuring three live productions and opportunities for community building. The event counts as a cultural exploration CLIPS experience for Honors College students.

photo.alt: Honors College students celebrate Shakespeare with annual Stratford Festival trip

stories.title: How many pilots does an F-16 carry? What we know about crashed jet
stories.summary: Residents in Grand Traverse County were ordered to evacuate after a Texas Air National Guard F-16 crashed near Blair Townhall Road, spilling hydrazine. The pilot ejected safely and is in stable condition. The evacuation was due to the hazardous chemical on board, and the jet was part of training at the Alpena Combat Readiness Training Center.

photo.alt: Portrait of Jalen Williams

stories.title: How the Gordie Howe Bridge is putting a historic Detroit landmark back on the map
stories.summary: Historic Fort Wayne, a sprawling military and Indigenous site along the Detroit River, is seeing increased foot traffic due to the new Gordie Howe International Bridge. Visitors using the bridge's pedestrian path are exploring the site, prompting city attention.

photo.alt: How the Gordie Howe Bridge is putting a historic Detroit landmark back on the map

stories.title: How to preapply for home repair help in Detroit
stories.summary: Detroit is accepting preapplications for its Critical Home Repair and LeadSafe Housing programs until Sept. 22, 2026. The city aims to repair 350 homes annually through these initiatives, prioritizing urgent issues like plumbing, accessibility barriers, and lead hazards. Income limits and eligibility criteria apply, with LeadSafe restricted to specific ZIP codes.

photo.alt: Abandoned house in Detroit needing repair

stories.title: How to preapply for home repair help in Detroit
stories.summary: Check if you’re eligible, then add your name to the list through Sept. 22.

photo.alt: How to preapply for home repair help in Detroit

stories.title: Hytek and Freshy Fine bring award-winning Lantz to new vapes
stories.summary: Detroit-based cannabis cultivator Hytek has partnered with Michigan brand Freshy Fine to launch a disposable CO2 oil vape featuring Lantz, an award-winning strain. The product, made with full-spectrum CO2 oil and cannabis-derived terpenes, will be available at multiple dispensaries across Michigan starting Sept. 18, 2026.

photo.alt: Hytek x Freshy Fine Lantz vape teaser image.

stories.title: 'It has broken my heart': Community members speak at U-M, Los Alamos data center town hall
stories.summary: Community members and University of Michigan officials gathered on Sept. 9 to discuss concerns about a $1.2 billion data center project between U-M and Los Alamos National Laboratory in Ypsilanti Township. Dozens of residents opposed the project during a town hall, expressing fears about its location near residential areas and questioning its impact. Project leaders acknowledged concerns but emphasized the facility's potential for research and less intrusive design compared to alternatives.

photo.alt: 'It has broken my heart': Community members speak at U-M, Los Alamos data center town hall

stories.title: 'It’s really devastating': Westland parishioners rally to keep weekend masses
stories.summary: The Archdiocese of Detroit is considering changes that could end weekend Masses at parishes across Southeast Michigan. Parishioners at St. Mary, Cause of Our Joy in Westland, have started a petition with over 400 signatures to oppose the proposal, which could begin in July 2027. Westland Mayor Kevin Coleman also supports the parish, highlighting its role in spiritual guidance and community connection.

photo.alt: 'It’s really devastating': Westland parishioners rally to keep weekend masses

stories.title: JD Power gives Detroit Metro high marks for satisfaction. Where it ranks
stories.summary: Detroit Metropolitan Airport ranked No. 2 among 'mega-sized' airports in the 21st North America Airport Satisfaction Study by JD Power, with a score of 663. Minneapolis-Saint Paul International Airport topped the list with 684 points, while Phoenix's Sky Harbor International Airport came third with 642 points. The study evaluated passenger satisfaction across airports categorized by size.

photo.alt: Portrait of Jenna Prestininzi

stories.title: Jet pilot stable after F-16 crash in Michigan
stories.summary: Residents in Northern Michigan were ordered to evacuate after an F-16 jet crash on Sept. 17, 2026. The pilot ejected safely and is in stable condition, with no other injuries reported. Authorities cited a hazardous chemical spill as the reason for the evacuation.

photo.alt: Portrait of Darcie Moran

stories.title: John Allison Retires as William F. Hosford Collegiate Professor of Materials Science and Engineering
stories.summary: John Allison, a renowned materials scientist and leader in Integrated Computational Materials Engineering (ICME), retires after a distinguished career spanning academia, industry, and national initiatives. His work helped pioneer the Materials Genome Initiative and led the PRISMS Center. With over 240 publications and five patents, he served as a professor at U-M since 2010 and held the William F. Hosford Collegiate Professor title since 2018.

source.name: University of Michigan Museum of Natural History

photo.alt: University of Michigan campus

stories.title: Joseph M. Messana to Retire from University of Michigan on September 30, 2026
stories.summary: Joseph M. Messana, professor of internal medicine at the University of Michigan Medical School, will retire on September 30, 2026. A U-M alumnus, he joined the faculty in 1988 and held leadership roles including nephrology clinical service chief and CEO of Michigan Dialysis Services. His work in health policy for End Stage Kidney Disease and teaching excellence earned him multiple awards, including the H. Marvin Pollard Award and Nephrology Teacher of the Year.

source.name: Joseph M. Messana
source.publication: University of Michigan Museum of Natural History

photo.alt: University of Michigan faculty recognition

stories.title: Judy Mousigian Nesmith to Retire from UM-Dearborn on June 30, 2026
stories.summary: Judy Mousigian Nesmith, lecturer IV in biological sciences at UM-Dearborn, will retire on June 30, 2026. With a 36-year career in undergraduate biology education, she modernized laboratory instruction, implemented active learning strategies, and supported students through roles like biology discipline adviser. Her work during the pandemic included adapting labs for remote learning.

source.name: Judy Mousigian Nesmith
source.publication: University of Michigan Museum of Natural History

photo.alt: University of Michigan faculty recognition

stories.title: Julie M. Ribaudo to Retire from University of Michigan on August 20, 2026
stories.summary: Julie M. Ribaudo, clinical professor of social work at the University of Michigan School of Social Work, will retire on August 20, 2026. With 22 years in social work practice and 18 years teaching, she earned awards like Professor of the Year and the 2026 Lifetime Achievement 2 Impact Award. Her community work includes leadership in infant mental health advocacy and service to young children and families.

source.name: Julie M. Ribaudo
source.publication: University of Michigan Museum of Natural History

photo.alt: University of Michigan faculty recognition

stories.title: Lawrence M. Seiford to Retire from University of Michigan on May 24, 2026
stories.summary: Lawrence M. Seiford, professor of industrial and operations engineering at the University of Michigan College of Engineering, will retire on May 24, 2026. A scholar in operations research and data envelopment analysis, he held leadership roles including chair of the Department of Industrial and Operations Engineering and co-director of the Tauber Institute for Global Operations. He received the Albert G. Holzman Distinguished Educator Award and is a fellow of multiple professional societies.

stories.summary: Margaret Carver, a global leader in infectious diseases and bioinorganic chemistry, retires after 40 years of contributions to pharmacy education and research. Her legacy includes 29 years on the admissions committee and twice receiving the COP Teaching Excellence Award.

stories.title: Michelin Guide Ceremony in Detroit Next April
stories.summary: The Michelin Guide is bringing its Great Lakes ceremony to Detroit next April, sparking questions about its impact on the local food scene. stories.title: Michigan AG candidate Doug Lloyd cut charges, sought no jail in sex-crime cases
stories.summary: A Metro Times investigation reveals that Republican Michigan AG candidate Doug Lloyd's office reduced charges or avoided jail in multiple sex-crime cases during his tenure as Eaton County prosecutor. The review includes instances involving underage victims, a former Olympic coach, and a domestic violence case linked to subsequent murders. The findings emerge as Lloyd faces Democrat Eli Savit in a closely contested race.

stories.title: Michigan asks nonprofits to supplement SNAP after federal cuts
stories.summary: The state is calling on nonprofits to support Michiganders affected by federal changes to the One Big Beautiful Bill Act, which alters work requirements and cuts funding for programs like Medicaid and SNAP. These changes take effect in January 2027. The State Health Department has allocated over $12 million in grants for nonprofits to provide community navigators to help residents apply for or renew coverage through the Healthy Michigan Plan or SNAP benefits.

photo.alt: SNAP assistance in Michigan

stories.title: Michigan diesel fuel prices hit record high
stories.summary: The price of diesel fuel in Michigan is the highest it’s ever been, with AAA reporting an average cost of $6.26 per gallon. This breaks the previous record of $6.20 set in May. Gasoline prices have also risen by 12 cents in a day, with regular unleaded averaging $4.43 per gallon, up 41 cents from a week ago.

photo.alt: Gas price record in Michigan

stories.title: Michigan football erupts in third quarter for blowout win over UTEP
stories.summary: Michigan football erupted for 28 points in the third quarter, leading to a 52-17 victory over UTEP. The win improved Kyle Whittingham’s team to 3-0 ahead of Big Ten play, with quarterback Bryce Underwood and receiver Andrew Marsh playing key roles in the decisive third-quarter surge.

stories.title: Michigan football stuns No. 11 Oklahoma 17-10 in statement victory at The Big House
stories.summary: The Michigan Wolverines upset the No. 11-ranked Oklahoma Sooners 17-10 in a home game at The Big House. Key contributors included quarterback Bryce Underwood, who rushed for a touchdown and passed for 111 yards, and punter Cameron Brown, whose strategic punting set up defensive stops. The victory marked Michigan's first win in the all-time series against Oklahoma, which was played for the first time at Michigan Stadium.

stories.title: Michigan gas prices soar to $4.89, some Metro Detroit stations top $5
stories.summary: Michigan's average gas price has reached $4.89, with some Metro Detroit stations exceeding $5. Diesel averages $6.67 per gallon, driven by high oil prices and a refinery outage. Experts attribute the surge to global factors including the war in Iran and reduced Russian diesel exports.

photo.alt: Michigan gas prices soar to $4.89, some Metro Detroit stations top $5

stories.title: Michigan launches project with crop insurance companies to reward regenerative farming
stories.summary: Michigan is launching a pilot project with crop insurance companies to reward regenerative farming practices. The program, involving about 80 farmers in the Thumb region, uses AI analysis and soil samples to assess lower crop loss risks, potentially reducing insurance costs. The initiative aims to promote healthier soil through techniques like cover crops and no-till planting, which can improve water retention and crop yields.

photo.alt: Early spring view of a Michigan farm.

stories.title: Michigan Lottery Daily 3, Daily 4 results for Sept. 19, 2026
stories.summary: The Michigan Lottery announced the winning numbers for the Daily 3 and Daily 4 games on September 19, 2026. Midday Daily 3 numbers were 9-5-3, and evening numbers were 1-1-4. For Daily 4, midday numbers were 9-0-3-5, and evening numbers were 2-6-1-8.

stories.title: Michigan Public names Brian Manzullo as managing editor of multiplatform news strategy
stories.summary: Michigan Public has appointed Brian Manzullo as its inaugural managing editor of multiplatform news strategy. Manzullo previously served as digital director at the Detroit Free Press for over 14 years. In his new role, he will lead digital journalism efforts to enhance the station's cross-platform reach and impact.

stories.title: Michigan regulators approve $74.52 million natural gas rate increase for DTE Energy
stories.summary: The Michigan Public Service Commission approved a $74.52 million natural gas rate increase for DTE Energy to fund system modernization. The commission also authorized a virtual power plant pilot program in Ann Arbor and increased power outage credits for customers.

stories.summary: Michigan's U.S. Senate candidates, Democrat Abdul El-Sayed and Republican Mike Rogers, present contrasting health care policies. El-Sayed advocates for Medicare for All, while Rogers emphasizes transparency and market-based solutions like cost disclosure and expanded TrumpRx. Rogers criticized Medicare for All as disruptive and highlighted prescription drug costs as a key issue.

photo.alt: Michigan U.S. Senate candidate Mike Rogers speaks to reporters at a campaign office in Taylor, Michigan on Saturday, September 19.

stories.title: Michigan State falls behind late in loss to No. 3 Notre Dame: Live updates recap
stories.summary: Michigan State fell to No. 3 Notre Dame 27-10 in a game dominated by the Fighting Irish. The Spartans were outgained 395-167 and struggled offensively, with quarterback Alessio Milivojevic throwing for 123 yards with two interceptions. Notre Dame's efficient offense, highlighted by a 68-yard touchdown drive, sealed the victory as MSU drops to 2-1 on the season.

stories.title: Michigan State struggles to keep pace in second half, falls at No. 3 Notre Dame

Notre Dame's CJ Carr and Micah Gilbert dominated, while Michigan State's Alessio Milivojevic threw two interceptions.

photo.alt: Notre Dame football hosts Michigan State in first rivalry matchup in nine years at Notre Dame Stadium in South Bend on Saturday, Sept. 19, 2026.

stories.title: Michigan Supreme Court orders review of Oxford school shooter's life without parole sentence
stories.summary: The Michigan Supreme Court has directed the Court of Appeals to review Ethan Crumbley's appeal of his life without parole sentence for the 2021 Oxford High School shooting. Crumbley, who was 15 at the time, pleaded guilty to 24 counts including first-degree murder. The case will focus on claims of ineffective trial counsel and procedural challenges to his sentence.

photo.alt: Oakland County Prosecutor Karen McDonald proceeds with an opening statement as defendant Ethan Crumbley, right, listens, Thursday, July 27, 2023, in Pontiac, Mich. stories.title: MichMash: Top 10 Michigan House seats that could flip in the 2026 midterms

stories.summary: Republican U.S. Senate candidate Mike Rogers proposed suspending state and federal gas taxes amid rising fuel prices, but Michigan House Speaker Matt Hall warned it would jeopardize a bipartisan road funding deal. Rogers criticized recent gas tax increases as 'unconscionable,' while Hall emphasized the revenue-neutral nature of last year's tax shift. Gas prices in Michigan averaged $4.75 per gallon as of Thursday, the 10th highest in the U.S.

stories.summary: A new select committee in the Michigan House was established to review the signature verification sampling process for ballot initiatives, following a deadlock on a voter ID petition. The committee, introduced by House Speaker Matt Hall, aims to ensure the process is followed correctly after the Board of State Canvassers rejected the petition due to a narrow margin in valid signatures.

stories.summary: The Michigan League for Public Policy released its 2026 Kids Count report, revealing declines in college readiness, education participation, and economic wellbeing for Michigan youth. The state ranks 32nd nationally for economic wellbeing and 42nd in education, with rising poverty and food insecurity rates among young adults. The report highlights policy recommendations to address these issues, including expanding the earned income tax credit and improving access to community college.

photo.alt: Arabia Simeon, founder and CEO of Politics on the Go discusses youth voter turnout at a panel discussion during the Michigan League for Public Policy's Champions for Kids luncheon on Sept. 17, 2026.

stories.summary: Two Oakland County malls, Great Lakes Crossing and Twelve Oaks, are adding new stores, restaurants, and attractions. stories.summary: A tornado with 115 mph winds caused damage in Detroit's eastside, including Belle Isle. stories.summary: The U.S. Forest Service is proposing to rescind the 2001 Roadless Rule, which would allow logging and road construction in protected national forests in Michigan. stories.title: Sheriff seeking help for surviving farm animals after sheep found dead on abandoned property
stories.summary: Genesee County Sheriff Christopher Swanson is seeking help for surviving farm animals after goats and sheep were found dead on an abandoned property in Mt. Morris Township. The sheriff's office received a tip on Sept. 18 about the animals being left with rotted hay and no water, and police discovered remains that were likely starved to death. stories.summary: Soldiers’ Angels is a national non-profit organization providing aid, comfort, and resources to military personnel, veterans, and their families. stories.summary: The City of Ann Arbor is considering a road diet for the Broadway Bridge and North Division Street. stories.title: South Lyon City Council directs staff to examine impacts of canceling Flock contract
stories.summary: The South Lyon City Council directed its staff to examine the legal and financial impacts of canceling the Flock contract for automated license plate reader cameras. stories.summary: Ann Arbor is touted as a top retirement destination. Retirees like Tracey Lind and Emily Ingalls chose the city for its affordability, cultural offerings, and healthcare access. stories.summary: City officials say opponents of proposed bike lanes on the Broadway Bridge in Ann Arbor are premature, while supporting an extension of bike lanes on Division Street. stories.summary: Lol Tolhurst, former drummer and co-founder of The Cure, will speak at Detroit's Recovery and Resilience Festival on substance use disorder and recovery. stories.title: U.S. Supreme Court ruled against Trump . . . for now
stories.summary: The U.S. Supreme Court upheld a preliminary injunction blocking the implementation of President Donald Trump's executive order on mail-in ballots, which would have required the U.S. Postal Service to transmit ballots only to voters on a national list. The ruling, which kept in place a Boston-based federal judge's injunction, cited concerns about insufficient time for election officials to comply with the rule before the November elections. A new Glengariff poll also shows declining voter confidence in Michigan's election system, with 74.4% of likely voters believing it is fair and accurate, down from 79.4% in 2025.

stories.title: Unless a buyer steps up, the Toledo Blade to print last edition at the end of the year

Block Communications cited financial losses as the reason for the decision, following rejected contract negotiations with the NewsGuild. The paper has a storied history, including Pulitzer Prizes and a role in local journalism, but faces potential closure amid industry challenges.

stories.title: Why this Detroit tenants lawsuit is making landlords nervous
stories.summary: The Detroit Tenants Union is suing the 36th District Court to block evictions and rent collection for properties lacking city-issued certificates of compliance. Landlords warn this could destabilize Detroit's rental market, while the union argues it will force property repairs. A hearing to dismiss the case is scheduled for September 21, 2026.

stories.title: Will winter be brutal? Don't look to these caterpillars for answers
stories.summary: The article explains that while folklore suggests woolly bear caterpillars can predict winter severity based on their band colors, experts from Michigan State University and the National Weather Service state that the band widths are determined by factors like hatching conditions and genetics, not weather. The caterpillars, which will become Isabella tiger moths, are often misunderstood as weather forecasters.

stories.title: With vote-by-mail court fight settled, attention shifts to protections at the polls
stories.summary: Voting rights groups and Democratic officials are preparing for potential election interference from the Trump administration by launching voter protection campaigns ahead of the midterm elections. Common Cause and the Democratic Party plan to deploy thousands of volunteers to polling sites across multiple states to counter efforts like voter intimidation and misinformation.

photo.alt: With vote-by-mail court fight settled, attention shifts to protections at the polls

stories.title: With vote-by-mail court fight settled, attention shifts to protections at the polls
stories.summary: Following the resolution of a court battle over vote-by-mail, efforts are now focused on ensuring election protections at polling stations. Trump's influence has fueled distrust in election results, with only 34% of adults trusting government certifications. Initiatives like voter advocate training and town hall events aim to counter disinformation and build trust in the election process.

stories.title: Woman, 67, killed in head-on crash in Branch County
stories.summary: Janet Murray, 67, was killed in a head-on collision on Sept. 18 in Quincy Township, Branch County. The other driver, a 51-year-old man from Coldwater, sustained minor injuries. Authorities are investigating the crash's cause.
